decided: When the AI would run an external review or a blind pair on its own but the user's work is not committed yet, it stops and tells the user the work is uncommitted, rather than committing the work for them; committing first is left to the stage's next change.
alternatives: have orbit itself check for uncommitted work and give that its own reason to stop
commit the work automatically before running the review
why: Stopping and saying why keeps this change small and never does anything the user did not ask for. The stop comes from the review's own instructions, which refuse to run on uncommitted work, so no new record lands and the AI sees no progress. Giving orbit's status its own reason for uncommitted work would mean the status reading the project's version history, which it does nowhere today; and committing for the user is new behaviour nobody has reviewed yet.
detail: Option A of the fresh system pass's dirty-tree finding (review-system-2026-11-09T23-04-10Z), ratified in chat 2026-11-09: 'c feels right to me. ok to do a first to keep things moving'. Option C (a commit of named paths before a chained external command) is carried to the stage's second change.
